senses.definition: A building for recreational use such as a hunting lodge or a summer cabin.
Ellipsis of porter's lodge: a building or room near the entrance of an estate or building, especially (UK, Canada) as a college mailroom.

quotes.text: [H]e walked across Hawthorn Tree Court on his way to the porter's lodge. […] At the lodge he cleared his pigeon-hole.
quotes.reference: 1991 September, Stephen Fry, chapter 2, in The Liar, London: Heinemann, →ISBN, section I, page 39:

senses.definition: A local chapter of some fraternities, such as freemasons.
(US) A local chapter of a trade union.
A rural hotel or resort, an inn.
A beaver's shelter constructed on a pond or lake.
A den or cave.
The chamber of an abbot, prior, or head of a college.
(mining) The space at the mouth of a level next to the shaft, widened to permit wagons to pass, or ore to be deposited for hoisting; called also platt.
A collection of objects lodged together.

quotes.text: the Maldives, a famous lodge of islands
quotes.reference: 1720, [Daniel Defoe], The Life, Adventures, and Pyracies, of the Famous Captain Singleton, London: […] J[ohn] Brotherton, […], J[ohn] Graves […], A[nne] Dodd, […], and T[homas] Warner, […], →OCLC:

senses.definition: A Native American home, such as tipi or wigwam.

subsenses.definition: (by extension) The people who live in one such home; a household.
(historical) A family of Native Americans, or the persons who usually occupy an Indian lodge; as a unit of enumeration, reckoned from four to six persons.
examples: The tribe consists of about two hundred lodges, that is, of about a thousand individuals.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To be firmly fixed in a specified position.
examples: The bullet missed its target and lodged in the bark of a tree.

senses.definition: (transitive) To firmly fix in a specified position.
examples: I've got some spinach lodged between my teeth.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To stay in a boarding-house, paying rent to the resident landlord or landlady.
examples: The detective Sherlock Holmes lodged in Baker Street.

senses.definition: (intransitive) To stay in any place or shelter.

quotes.text: Stay and lodge by me this night.

senses.definition: (transitive) To supply with a room or place to sleep in for a time.
(transitive) To put money, jewellery, or other valuables for safety.
(transitive, chiefly law, politics) To place (a statement, etc.) with the proper authorities (such as courts, etc.).

senses.definition: (intransitive) To become flattened, as grass or grain, when overgrown or beaten down by the wind.
examples: The heavy rain caused the wheat to lodge.

senses.definition: (transitive) To cause to flatten, as grass or grain.
